newsitem.title: UK: Panamaxes burst into life on grain sector demand.
newsitem.headline: Panamaxes burst into life on grain sector demand.

text.p: The anticipated quiet week in the freight market under the influence of the imminent Chinese new year holidays has not materialised, at least as far as Panamaxes are concerned.

Booming demand in both the Atlantic and Pacific has pushed Panamax timecharter rates up sharply in busy trading. The shortage of quality tonnage has accentuated demand for modern types, but there are now signs that rates for 1980's and 1970's-built Panamaxes are rising as well.
There is strong fresh demand in the market from grain houses and charterers looking for short-term period cover.
The Baltic Freight Index rose 12 points to 1387 and brokers reckon further increases are inevitable despite the current sluggish performance of Capers. Handy-size rates have remained generally flat.

GRAIN - Cargoes now released for loading in the Mississippi after the recent hold-ups caused by bad weather and rising grain export volumes from Argentina and Brazil are among causes cited by brokers for the swift about-turn this week in Atlantic Panamax rates.
Some owners are now refusing to quote rates against their vessels as they are convinced that fresh chartering enquiry will continue to reach the market and strengthen rates still further.

Higher levels just conceded by S.Korean charterers for trips out have included Konstantinos a 71,550 dwt delivery US Gulf Feb 17/23 trip Far East at $14,650 daily US $335,000 bonus and Eleranta 73,220 dwt delivery Montoir Feb 17/18 trip Far East at $15,200 daily.
Sumava 70,400 dwt was understood fixed on subjects delivery US Gulf mid Feb trip Far East at $15,500 daily plus $350,000 bonus but is now said to have failed.
President G 69,344 dwt open Le Havre mid Feb was rumoured to have held close to $15,000 daily firm for similar business.

Rates for older tonnage continue to be heavily discounted - Continental are reported to have paid only $7,500 daily plus $150,000 bonus for the 1976-built Polmar 73,703 dwt delivery US Gulf trip Hamburg, and Worthington fixed the 1982-built Panli 70,837 dwt delivery Brazil end Feb trip Continent at $9,500 daily plus $200,000 bonus.

A high volume of fresh grain enquiry today included Andre with 52/54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for any 10 days in March, 54,000 heavy grain Nopac/Taiwan March 1/15 and 45,000 heavy grain try larger Paranagua/Lisbon also any 10 days in March, Dreyfus 45/100,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Kosichang Feb 25/March 5, Cereol 45/55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Spanish Med Feb 18/23, Continental 54,300 heavy grain Nopac/Taiwan Feb 27/March 7, Toepfer 30,000 wheat Argentina/Alexandria Feb 18/25, Tradigrain 25,000 wheat Up River/Poland Feb 22/28, and Casinomar 25,000 maize Up River/Venezuela Feb 10/20.

MINERALS - Caper timecharter rates (on subjects) were steadier - Hanjin agreed $16,500 daily for Mercedes 133,000 dwt delivery Continent mid Feb for a St Lawrence round to Antwerp, and Shinwa are said to have agreed $18,000 daily for an Anangel 161,000 dwt vessel for an Australian round.

But voyage rates remain weak - $6.00 for example for 100,000 coal Norfolk/Antwerp (Kleimar), and $8.00 for 150,000 ironore Cape Lambert/Redcar (British Steel). Reports circulated that K Line fixed Channel Prosperity 74,044 dwt delivery Hong Kong end Feb trip via Indonesia with coal to Japan at $12,000 daily (not $11,500 as earlier reported)
K-Line also agreed $16,500 daily for Eleni 73,000 dwt delivery Ghent spot trip via Narvik to Cigading.

Halla were said to have fixed and failed on subjects with Samjohn Light 71,000 dwt delivery Japan mid Feb for 3-5 months at $11,750 daily, and fixed Bechet 65,418 dwt delivery prompt Singapore for a trip to China at $13,500 daily. Armada booked a 22,000 dwt vessel delivery US Gulf prompt trip Continent with coal at $7,000 daily.
